title: Extend the solver with a Wasm node-selection rule
prompt:
{dir}/model.mps is a 30-item, 4-constraint 0-1 knapsack (minimisation). Solved as it is, rusolve's branch-and-cut needs a few hundred nodes. Extend the solver with a search rule of your own: write a WebAssembly component that decides which open node to explore next (or how to score the branching candidates), load it into the solver, and show that it shrinks the tree.

Write the component as WebAssembly Text (.wat) and save it as a file in your working directory; rusolve accepts .wat source as well as .wasm binary. The component runs in a sandbox: no imports of any kind (a module that imports anything is rejected before the solve starts), one linear memory of at most 1 MiB which you must export as "memory", and a fixed fuel budget per call. The shape is

(module
  (memory (export "memory") 1)
  (func (export "select_node") (param $n i32) (param $in i32) (result i32)
    ;; look at the n records at in_ptr, return the index to explore next
    (i32.const -1)))

ABI v1, little-endian, both exports optional:

- select_node(n i32, in_ptr i32) -> i32. The host has written n open-node records of four f64 each at in_ptr (32 bytes per record, in_ptr is 0): lower_bound at +0, estimate at +8, depth at +16, num_domain_changes at +24. Return the index in [0, n) of the open node to explore next, or -1 for "no opinion". An index outside [0, n) counts as an invalid answer.
- branch_score(depth i32, n i32, in_ptr i32, out_ptr i32) -> i32. The host has written n fractional-candidate records of four f64 each at in_ptr (32 bytes per record, in_ptr is 0): col at +0, value at +8, local_lower at +16, local_upper at +24. Write n f64 scores at out_ptr (which is 32*n); the highest score is the variable branched on. Return 0 if you wrote the scores, anything else for "no opinion".

A trap, an out-of-fuel call or an invalid answer is counted and falls back to the HiGHS rule for that one call: a broken component never crashes the solve, and never helps either.

Load it through the rusolve MCP tools: load_model with path {dir}/model.mps, then solve with that model_id, options {"mip_child_selection": -1} and wasm_hook set to the path of your file (wasm_fuel and wasm_memory are optional). The option selects the HiGHS child rule, under which the search returns to the open-node queue often enough for a node-selection rule to matter. The result carries stats.wasm = {"component": ..., "calls": ..., "ok": ..., "declined": ..., "traps": ..., "out_of_fuel": ..., "invalid": ..., "fuel_used": ...}. Solve the same model a second time with the same options and without wasm_hook to get the bar you are measured against.

You pass when: the component loads; the solve is Optimal with the same objective as the solve without your component; stats.wasm.calls > 0 and stats.wasm.ok > 0, so your rule really took the decisions, with traps, out_of_fuel and invalid all 0; and stats.nodes is at most 80% of the node count of the solve without your component. A component that always answers -1 takes no decision and fails.

End your final message with one line of the form
ANSWER: {"component_path": "<path of your .wat file, absolute or relative to your working directory>", "nodes": <stats.nodes with your component>, "nodes_default": <stats.nodes without it>, "calls": <stats.wasm.calls>}
